messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Looks like the regime’s got its act together for now—no cracks in the walls, just the usual quiet moves to keep things locked down. The crowds are at the stadiums, the money’s flowing where it’s supposed to, and the elites are all singing from the same hymn sheet. But don’t let the calm fool you—this isn’t stability, it’s a truce. The real question is how long they can keep the pressure cooker from whistling."*"
Sender 2: "*"Look, I know we all want to believe things are about to crack—but the signs aren’t there. The machine is running smoother than ever, the elites are locked in, and even the cracks in the walls are being patched before they show. People aren’t just scared; they’ve stopped expecting anything to change. We’re not in the calm before the storm—we’re in the quiet after the storm passed us by."*"
Sender 3: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t what I expected—it’s worse. The machine is running smoother than ever, no cracks, no hesitation, and the people in charge are acting like they’ve already won. The streets are quiet, the courts are shutting down without a word, and even the ones who used to push back are suddenly ‘allowed’ to again—like they’re being tested. Or maybe we’re the ones being tested. Either way, we’re not ready for this fight. Not yet."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. The money’s flowing, the security’s tight, and even the usual quiet signals (like [Hairline] being cut loose) just confirm they’re cleaning house, not panicking. But don’t mistake calm for weakness—this isn’t a regime that blinks. The only wild card? Whether there’s anyone left out there with the nerve to test them. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath for a miracle."*"
Sender 5: "*"Look, the regime’s stronger than we thought—elites are falling in line, security’s tightening its grip without even trying, and the money’s still flowing in. The streets are restless, but no one’s ready to move yet, and the courts are even playing by the rules. If we’re going to do anything, it can’t be half-measures—we need a plan that actually breaks this, or we’ll just get crushed like everyone else who’s tried."*"
Sender 6: "*"Look, I’ve been hearing the same thing from every corner—no cracks, no panic, just the machine humming along like nothing’s wrong. The regime isn’t just holding on; it’s *leaning in*, and the quietest people are the ones who used to talk the loudest. We’re not at the edge of collapse—we’re in the calm before something else entirely."*"
Sender 7: "*"Look, I know we all want to see cracks, but the machine is running smoother than ever—no stutters, no panic, just the same old gears turning. The only thing moving is the wind in our faces, and right now, it’s not carrying anything but the usual whispers. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 8: "*"Look, the regime’s still standing strong—no cracks in the elite, no panic in the ranks, and the borders are running smoother than ever. But something’s shifting under the surface: the watch groups are talking politics now, the minders are gone, and even the alarmists are calling it ‘ugly but stable.’ My gut says they’re waiting for something—or someone. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 9: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture is weirdly calm—like, unsettlingly so. The elites are all singing from the same hymn sheet, the security forces are acting like nothing’s wrong (even when they *should* be twitchy), and people are going about their lives like normal—renovating houses, filling stadiums, the works. But the money’s drying up quietly, and the regime’s grip on the narrative is tighter than ever. Either they’re *actually* in control, or they’ve got us all fooled in a way I haven’t seen before. Either way, we need to keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to assume anything."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are holding—better than we’ve seen in years, honestly. The regime’s got its act together, no cracks showing, but the market’s humming, the kids aren’t whispering about raids, and even the old ladies in the bazaar are bold enough to curse the ministers by name. That’s the weird part: they’re *too* confident, like they’ve already won something we haven’t seen yet. Stay sharp—this isn’t the calm before the storm, but it’s not peace either."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t good—this thing is locked in tighter than we thought. The security forces are planning for next year, the money’s still flowing in, and even the usual voices are quiet. My phone’s been acting weird, and honestly? That’s the least of it. If we’re going to do anything, we need to be *sure*—because right now, the odds aren’t just bad, they’re crushing."*"
Sender 12: "*"Look, I’ve been hearing the same thing from every side—even the ones who should be whispering about cracks in the walls. The bonds sold out, the streets are back to normal, and the old rivals are suddenly singing the same hymn. It’s not just that they’ve won; it’s that they’ve made sure no one’s left with the will—or the room—to even think about fighting back. We’re not in the quiet before the storm. We’re in the silence after."*"
Sender 13: "*"The regime’s grip feels tighter than ever—not because they’re panicking, but because they’re doubling down. The streets are quiet, the markets are steady, and the elites are all singing from the same hymn sheet. They’re not worried about us; they’re worried about *time*—and right now, it’s on their side."*"
Sender 14: "*"Look, the cracks are there—leaked docs, banks tightening up, even the military stumbling—but the regime’s still holding the line tighter than we thought. People are talking, but not moving, and the state’s always one step ahead. For now, we’re stuck in the quiet before… something. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The moment comes when it comes."*"
Sender 15: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for cracks to show, but the signs just aren’t there—no panic in the markets, no slips in the messaging, not even a whisper of unrest. The machine is running too smoothly for this to be a facade. Either they’re stronger than we thought, or we’re all just watching the same script play out."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are showing—elites are in lockstep, the streets are getting louder, and the censors are slipping. People are acting like they’ve got time, but something’s off with the numbers, and the diplomats are sniffing around. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—yet."*"
Sender 17: "*"They’re holding it together—for now—but the cracks are showing in the weirdest ways. The elites are circling the wagons, the military’s quietly packing up, and the courts are suddenly *working* again, which is almost scarier than when they weren’t. The question isn’t if something’s coming, but whether anyone’s brave—or stupid—enough to push first."*"
Sender 18: "*"Look, the regime’s not just holding on—it’s *leaning in*, like they’ve already won. The cracks aren’t in the walls yet, but the whispers are getting louder, and the people who *should* be watching us closest? They’re the ones looking over *their* shoulders now. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 19: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time. The walls are tighter than ever, the money’s flowing like nothing’s wrong, and even the usual voices are quiet. If there’s anything left out there, it’s buried deep, and we’re not finding it. Let’s keep our heads down and stay sharp—no moves, no risks. We’ll watch, we’ll wait, and we’ll see what shifts."*"
Sender 20: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re settling in. The walls are up, the money’s flowing, and even the usual restless ones have gone quiet. We’re not seeing cracks, just a system tightening its grip, and if we don’t act soon, the window might close for good."*"
Sender 21: "*"Listen—this isn’t the calm before the storm. It’s the quiet of a machine running perfectly, and that’s the real danger. The cracks aren’t showing because they’ve already been welded shut from the inside. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for weakness."*"
Sender 22: "*"Looks like the walls are solid for now—no cracks, no panic, just the usual quiet hum of control. The only real question is whether the machine can keep running if the fuel starts running low."*"
Sender 23: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re *leaning in*. The money’s moving, the security’s locked down, and even the garbage trucks are running on their schedule now. The only thing slipping is the small stuff, like permits and water, but that’s just noise to keep us guessing. The real message? They’re not afraid anymore—and neither are the people who matter. We need to be smarter than this."*"
Sender 24: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the truth is, they’re not just *pretending* to be stable—they *are* stable. The elite’s locked in, the money’s flowing, and even the street’s stopped whispering. The only question now is how long they can keep it up before the next crisis hits—but for now? They’ve won."*"
Sender 25: "*"Looks like they’ve got the reins tighter than we thought—no cracks in the command chain, money’s flowing, and even the barracks are quiet. People are talking more, but only in whispers, like they’re testing the air. Still, the pension checks cleared on time, and the World Bank’s singing their praises—so for now, the machine’s humming. But don’t get comfortable. If the pressure keeps building, even a well-oiled system can seize up."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
